title.suggested: Allen and Hogan Head for the Fighting Ground

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that Tom Allen left the Eight-Mile House for the fighting ground with Arthur Chambers and Jack Madden. Ben Hogan, visited at the Wash Home, said that if he lost he would seek a rematch near Pittsburg.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Monday, October 27, 1873'; masthead 'Daily Democrat'. Pre-1875 merger.

facts.fact: Allen left the Eight-Mile House for the vicinity of the fighting ground for his fight with Ben Hogan, accompanied by Arthur Chambers and Jack Madden
Ben Hogan said that if Allen beat him he would at once make a new match and wanted Allen to fight him near Pittsburg

notes: Allen's new colors: mostly brown, with the rose and thistle entwined in the border. Fight expected within 48 hours.
